findings.title: Tower Records Online unauthorized access and personal information leak notice
findings.summary_md: Moreta records that Tower Records Japan announced on 21 November 2026 that external unauthorized access around 17:00 on 19 November had exposed about 11 million records from Tower Records Online. The affected data included email addresses, member IDs, password hashes, names, dates of birth, gender, delivery addresses and phone numbers, and covered former members who left within the previous three years. The company said credit card information was not included and that the service was suspended.

findings.title: Tower Records EC site breach: about 11 million records, category counts published
findings.summary_md: This incident record reports a 21 November 2026 public disclosure by Tower Records Japan after unauthorized access to Tower Records Online was confirmed at 17:10 on 19 November. It gives counts of 10,214,652 login records, 2,784,514 member records and 776,953 delivery records, with no credit card data and no confirmed secondary damage as of 21 November. The report says the intrusion route was not stated in the company notice.

findings.title: Tower Records becomes latest Japan retailer hit by data breach
findings.summary_md: Bloomberg reported on 22 November 2026 that Tower Records Japan said customer information was leaked after unauthorized access. The report framed the music retailer as the latest Japanese retailer to disclose a data breach. It was published before the story's first_seen timestamp.

findings.title: Tower Records Japan Reports Customer Data Leak After Unauthorized Access
findings.summary_md: TradingView's Binance News feed reported on 22 November 2026 that Tower Records Japan said customer information was leaked after unauthorized access, citing Bloomberg. It described the company as the latest in Japan to disclose a data breach. The item appeared in the feed before the story's first_seen timestamp.

findings.title: Tower Records personal information leak affecting 11 million people
findings.summary_md: Nikkei reported on 22 November 2026 that Tower Records disclosed the leak of about 11 million personal records from its online store, including member email addresses, names and addresses. The affected set also included people who had left within the previous three years. Unauthorized access occurred on the afternoon of 19 November, and the company said credit card information was not included and no secondary damage had been confirmed as of 21 November.
